vendor: Redash (open-source project; originally Redash Ltd., acquired by Databricks, Inc. in June 2020, rebooted as a community-led project since April 2023)
product_family: Open-source SQL client and dashboarding/BI tool for connecting to and visualizing data from SQL, NoSQL, Big Data, and API data sources. Historically also offered a managed hosted service (app.redash.io), which was discontinued; today it is distributed solely as self-hosted, community-maintained software.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type I
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence: redash.io has no trust center or security page; the Privacy Policy (redash.io/privacy) and Terms of Service (redash.io/terms) contain no mention of SOC 2, and the GitHub security policy (getredash/redash) covers only vulnerability disclosure via email, with no compliance certifications mentioned.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence: same as SOC 2 Type I above; no trust center, security page, or SOC 2 report exists on redash.io.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on redash.io, redash.io/privacy, redash.io/terms, or the GitHub security policy. No ISO 27001 certificate or statement is published by the vendor.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a HIPAA attestation, BAA offering, or compliance statement on any redash.io page reviewed. Note: the hosted service that would have processed customer data on Redash's own servers (app.redash.io) was shut down effective November 30, 2021, so today's self-hosted-only distribution model places HIPAA responsibility entirely on the customer's own deployment.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence Redash itself holds PCI DSS. The Privacy Policy lists Stripe as a third-party payment processor ('Redash uses selected third parties... Stripe...'); PCI DSS, if applicable, belongs to Stripe as the payment subprocessor, not Redash.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Redash is a SQL/BI dashboarding tool, not an AI model provider, and no AI-governance certification is referenced anywhere on redash.io.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a CSA STAR registry entry or self-assessment for Redash on redash.io or the GitHub project pages.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a FedRAMP authorization for Redash.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a formal GDPR compliance statement on the current redash.io/privacy page (it does not use the word 'GDPR'). A now-unreachable Redash blog post (blog.redash.io, subdomain no longer resolves) was previously reported by third parties as saying the privacy policy was already GDPR-compliant, but this could not be confirmed on a current vendor-owned page.

privacy.ai_training_note: Not applicable in the conventional sense: Redash is a SQL client / BI dashboarding tool, not an AI model, and there is no evidence it trains any AI/ML model on customer data. No DPA is offered on the current site; the only past DPA-relevant context was for the now-discontinued hosted service (app.redash.io, shut down November 30, 2021, with all hosted customer data deleted within 30 days per the vendor's own EOL FAQ). For today's self-hosted-only distribution, there is no ongoing customer data relationship with the vendor to process, so no DPA is published.
privacy.data_region: Redash is distributed as self-hosted software, so the customer's own infrastructure determines data region. The Privacy Policy names AWS and Google Cloud among third-party service providers used for redash.io's own web properties, but no specific region commitment is stated.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: Redash is self-hosted; the vendor publishes an HTTPS/SSL setup guide for admins to configure TLS on their own instance, but does not itself guarantee encryption in transit since it does not operate the customer's deployment

security.name: Password/credential storage
security.value: Terms of Service state passwords are 'retained at Redash's servers using standard security practices' for accounts on Redash-operated properties; database connection credentials entered into a self-hosted instance are stored by that instance per the admin's own configuration (see Secret Keys documentation)

security.name: Data retention
security.value: Terms of Service state Redash 'may not retain information for more than 30 days' except as specified in membership plans, for data on Redash-operated web properties

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure
security.value: Security issues can be reported to security@redash.io, with PGP encryption available via a published key; the policy is limited in scope to disclosure handling and does not describe pen testing cadence or formal compliance controls

security.name: Historical security incident disclosure
security.value: Vendor has publicly disclosed at least one past security release (v4.0.2) via its own blog, indicating a practice of public vulnerability disclosure for the open-source project

security.name: Hosted service status
security.value: The only Redash-operated hosted/managed service (app.redash.io) was shut down effective November 30, 2021, with all customer data deleted within 30 days; there is currently no Redash-operated production hosting of customer data

products.name: Redash (self-hosted, open source)
products.category: Self-hosted SQL client and BI/dashboarding tool
products.data_scope: Runs entirely on customer-controlled infrastructure; the Redash project/maintainers have no access to customer data or database credentials by default
products.notes: BSD-2-Clause licensed; the only actively distributed edition since the hosted service EOL'd in Nov 2021; development is community-led (volunteer maintainers) as of April 2023 and described by third-party sources as largely frozen/slow-moving compared to alternatives like Metabase or Apache Superset

products.name: Redash Cloud / app.redash.io (hosted, discontinued)
products.category: Formerly a Redash-managed hosted SQL/BI service
products.data_scope: Previously ran on Redash-operated servers; customer data was stored on Redash infrastructure
products.notes: Shut down effective November 30, 2021; all hosted customer data was deleted within 30 days thereafter per the vendor's own FAQ. Not a currently purchasable or usable product. Any certification claims tied to this legacy hosted service should be treated as historical/inapplicable, not current.

compare.pricing_model: Free, open-source, self-hosted software (BSD-2-Clause license); no current paid hosted tier since app.redash.io was discontinued in 2021
compare.data_residency: Fully customer-controlled, since Redash is self-hosted-only; no vendor-operated data region applies

flags: Redash was acquired by Databricks, Inc. in 2020, but is now a community-led open-source project (per an April 2023 GitHub announcement) with no clear ongoing formal commercial backing. Databricks' own enterprise certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and others for the Databricks platform) do not extend to the standalone Redash open-source project.

The only Redash-operated hosted service that would have made vendor-side certifications meaningful (app.redash.io) was discontinued in November 2021; today's self-hosted-only distribution model means most security/compliance posture (encryption, access control, HIPAA suitability, data residency) is entirely determined by each customer's own deployment, not by Redash the vendor.

Multiple 2025-2026 third-party sources describe Redash open-source development as largely frozen or slow compared to actively maintained alternatives (e.g., Metabase, Apache Superset), which may affect how promptly any future vulnerability would be patched.
